title: Carat weight
text: Carat measures weight, not the visible size of a diamond. One metric carat is 200 milligrams and is divided into 100 points. Larger carat weight can affect price, but color, clarity and cut also matter.

title: Diamond cut
text: Cut describes how a diamond's proportions, facets and craftsmanship affect its interaction with light. GIA's cut grades from Excellent to Poor apply to standard round brilliant diamonds. The dataset uses Fair, Good, Very Good, Premium and Ideal; those dataset categories are not the same as GIA's cut grades.

title: Diamond color
text: The GIA D-to-Z scale grades how much color is present in a diamond, with D at the colorless end and increasing color toward Z. The project dataset includes only grades D through J.

title: Diamond clarity
text: Clarity grading considers the number, size, location and visibility of inclusions and blemishes. GIA's clarity scale has 11 grades from Flawless to Included, assessed using 10x magnification. This dataset contains a subset of those grades: I1, SI2, SI1, VS2, VS1, VVS2, VVS1 and IF.

title: Price estimates
text: This project estimates listed prices from examples in its training dataset. It is for learning and comparison, not a certified appraisal. Compare diamonds with similar attributes and check grading reports before buying.

title: Price per carat
text: Price per carat is calculated as listed price divided by carat weight. In this project it is used only for descriptive analysis. It is not a prediction input because it contains the target price.

title: Unusual measurements and listings
text: An anomaly flag means a record differs from patterns in the data. It does not prove fraud. Check the dimensions, original listing and grading certificate.

title: Model feature importance
text: The project uses permutation importance and SHAP to describe how the trained model uses its input features. These methods explain model behaviour; they do not prove that a feature causes a price change.
